tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Create ONE new script + test. Do NOT git commit/branch/push/stash. No MCP, no network, no model calls, no sends. STRICTLY READ-ONLY over the repo: the script must never write or mutate any pipeline state (writing its own report to stdout or an --output path is the only output).

GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 6 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing (it runs the tests AND executes the script against the repo's real episodes dir).

OWNED FILES (only these — both new):
  scripts/funnel_status.py
  tests/test_funnel_status.py

WHY. The owner's question, verbatim: "how do i know this whole funnel is running from
prospecting to editing to publication to referrals?" Today the answer is scattered
across six surfaces (tick JSON, queue module, DAG projection, referral ledger, autonomy
ladder, department outbox). This script is the single answer: one command, one screen,
every funnel stage with its live number and its health.

BUILD scripts/funnel_status.py — a read-only aggregator over modules that ALL already
exist (read each before wiring; import them, do not reimplement logic):
  * PROSPECTING: candidate_ingest.load_candidate_feed — candidates by kind, feed
    problems. Outreach posture from pipeline_queue.queue_status via
    loop_runner.assemble_world (count/target/healthy/should_outreach/stalled).
  * PRODUCTION: per episode (skip killed ones by default; --all shows them):
    directory name, stage, and the DAG audit one-liner from
    episode_evidence.audit_episode — complete / N silent skips / N authorized.
  * PUBLICATION: episodes with publish_date in the next 14 days (id, date, stage),
    plus the most recently published episode.
  * PROMOTION: the drumbeat portion of a DRY plan — call loop_tick.plan_tick on the
    assembled world and list planned promotion_touch actions (episode, kind, why)
    and the skipped list. Planning is pure; this stays read-only.
  * REFERRALS: episodes/REFERRALS.json (schema referral-ledger-v1) — asks sent
    (count + per-guest state + days since ask), referrals recorded/introduced/
    converted. Absent file = section says so plainly.
  * SEND SWITCHES: lane_autonomy.load_committed_lane_levels — each lane and its
    committed level, flagging any lane at L-policy as LIVE.
  * WATCHDOG: the newest dag_supervisor observation from
    /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/departments/podcast/state/observations.jsonl
    (status + metrics + age), and the count of open items in
    departments/podcast/state/decisions_outbox.jsonl. Missing files = the section
    reports the absence, never crashes. Accept a --state-dir override so tests use
    tmp dirs.
  OUTPUT: default a compact human screen — one section per stage above, each section
  ONE to FIVE lines, plain words, numbers first (the owner reads this on a phone).
  --json emits the full structure. Every section that cannot be computed states WHY
  in place (e.g. "referral ledger: missing"). Exit 0 always when the report renders;
  exit 2 when any section reports a red condition (silent skips, stalled episodes,
  feed problems, watchdog alarm) so cron can alert on it.

TESTS (tests/test_funnel_status.py; at least 6, tmp dirs, no network):
 (1) a healthy fixture (episodes with evidence, candidates file, referrals ledger,
     ok watchdog observation) renders every section and exits 0;
 (2) NEGATIVE: an episode with a silent skip flips exit to 2 and the production
     section names the episode;
 (3) NEGATIVE: missing REFERRALS.json and missing observations file render "missing"
     lines and never raise;
 (4) --json output is valid JSON containing all seven sections;
 (5) the promotion section reflects the dry plan (a fixture catalog episode with an
     on-disk clip appears as a planned touch);
 (6) NEGATIVE: the script performs no writes — run it over a fixture tree and assert
     the tree's file list and mtimes are unchanged;
 (7) killed episodes are hidden by default and shown with --all.
